title: One Thing About Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) That You Probably Didn't Realize
text:
Warren Buffett isn't the only force of nature with deep pockets that loves buying Apple's ( AAPL ) stock.
Apple can't get enough of itself, either.
Through its joy of buying back its shares, UBS estimates that Apple has historically accounted for 1% to 4% of the stock's daily trading volume. Now that is betting on yourself day in, and day out.
It's unlikely such an appetite will down down anytime soon -- in fact, it may grow stronger.
UBS estimates that Apple maintains a net cash position of $163 billion, or $125 billion net of an expected $38 billion tax payment related to the new tax reform plan. With Apple's expectation it will reduce net cash to zero over time, UBS thinks Apple can buy 1.5 million to 2 million shares per day and be at, or under, 5% of daily trading volume. Assuming an 8% annual appreciation of the stock, Apple could buy 10% of its shares over four years and reach net cash position of zero by fiscal year 2021.
As it stands, Apple will be battling Warren Buffett for the best price on those shares. The billionaire's holding conglomerate Berkshire Hathaway ( BRK.A ) hiked its stake in Action Alerts Plus holding Apple by a whopping 23% to 165.3 million shares, according to a new 13F filing on Wednesday.
Source: UBS
